concepts.def: UN scheme paying countries to keep forests standing.
Combining trees with crops or livestock on same land.
Removing only some trees, leaving the canopy intact.
Low-impact tourism funding conservation and locals.
Labels like FSC indicating sustainable timber.

walkthroughs.body_html: REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation) pays tropical countries based on measured forest carbon retained. Norway has paid billions to Brazil and Indonesia. Challenges include accurate measurement, ensuring permanence and avoiding leakage where deforestation shifts elsewhere. Done well, it makes living forests worth more than felled ones.

Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock. Shade-grown coffee under rainforest canopies, alley cropping rows of maize between hedges, and silvopasture combining trees with grazing all build soil, cut erosion and sequester carbon. Yields can match monoculture while boosting biodiversity and resilience to drought.

Selective logging takes only mature, valuable trees and leaves the canopy mostly intact. With careful planning, road minimisation and 30 year cutting cycles, it can yield timber while keeping forest function. FSC certification verifies practice. Compared with clear-cutting, selective logging keeps around 60 to 80 percent of biodiversity intact.
